plain: One strong impression of a person or thing spills over into how every other quality gets rated.
eli5: Someone is great at football, so you guess they must be good at maths too.
technical: Thorndike's (1920) “constant error”: ratings of conceptually separate traits correlate more strongly than the traits themselves, because a global impression leaks into each dimension. For an LLM judge, one salient feature (fluency, confidence) inflates every rubric criterion.

m.hire: A confident handshake raises the interviewer's score for coding as well as communication.
m.review: One big launch lifts the manager's rating on teamwork and planning too.
m.wine: A gorgeous nose makes the judge score the finish higher as well.
m.med: A reader impressed by one clear finding reads the rest of the film as more certain.
m.ump: A pitcher with a reputation for command gets the borderline calls.
